questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:

options.text: A person involved with a traffic study.

questions.explanation: You must always yield to a pedestrian who is blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at one-way streets and ramps. It tells you not to drive in that direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp right turn in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that there is a sharp right turn ahead.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, it is important to remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.
Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.
Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles do.
Require less time to pass on an incline than smaller vehicles do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and heavier. They need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: When you approach a stop sign without a crosswalk, you should stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line if there is one. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate is lowered.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Not pay attention to how many tracks there are to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop for trains or other rail vehicles.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no warning signals, a driver should slow down, look, and listen.
questions.explanation: If there are no warning lights or gates, slow down and look both ways along the tracks. Listen for a train. Only cross when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming. Be ready for traffic from other directions.

questions.question: On a freeway, you realize you missed your turn or exit. You should:

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane of travel.
Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or other location where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or other location where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: Do not back up on a freeway or shoulder. Continue to the next exit or safe place to turn around.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: You must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when you can.

questions.question: A professional truck driver must:

options.text: Have a valid commercial driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a valid commercial driver license.
questions.explanation: A commercial driver license (CDL) lets you drive tractor-trailers, passenger buses, tank trucks, school buses with 16 or more people, and vehicles carrying hazardous materials. A regular driver license only allows you to drive vehicles and small trucks under 26,001 pounds that do not need a CDL.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not drive under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (in this case, 13 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: Your license will be revoked or suspended if you:

options.text: Make a false statement to the DMV.
Take a driver license test for another person.

questions.explanation: The DMV or a court can revoke or suspend your license if you are convicted of certain crimes. These include making false statements to the DMV, running from police, and taking a driver license test for someone else.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed under good road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe speed under all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed under good road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the posted limit for safety. When conditions are bad, you should slow down.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train. You must stop:

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if red lights are flashing, a crossing gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible or too close to cross safely. When unsure, stop. Never try to beat a train.

questions.question: Orange is the color of signs used in construction work zones.
questions.explanation: Most signs in work zones are orange and diamond-shaped, though some are rectangular. These signs are often reflective so they stand out at night.

questions.question: In which of the following ways can alcohol affect you?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. You may feel more confident and lively, but your thinking is unclear. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, coordination, and balance. Your vision and ability to judge distance get worse, making it hard to react to what is around you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells you that an intersection is coming up.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signals let other drivers know your plans and help prevent accidents.

questions.question: Your driver license can be revoked or suspended if you are convicted of:

options.text: Driving a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
Making a false statement to the DMV.
Committing a felony using a motor vehicle.

questions.explanation: The DMV or a court can suspend or revoke your driver license for several offenses. These include driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs, making false statements to the DMV, and committing a felony with a motor vehicle.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, you should:

options.text: Be ready to react to road hazards.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready to react to unexpected hazards. Do not look at any one thing for more than a few seconds to avoid highway hypnosis.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, you should wait until the entire car is visible in your rearview mirror before moving back to the right lane.
questions.explanation: After passing another vehicle, do not return to your original lane until the entire vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. Driving after alcohol or drugs is unsafe. Mixing them is even more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is threatening you or driving dangerously, stay calm. Slow down and let them pass. Keep distance between your vehicles. Do not make eye contact or obscene gestures.

questions.question: You cannot pass another vehicle:
questions.explanation: You cannot pass another vehicle on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. These are unsafe and illegal locations to pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:

options.text: Driving more slowly than normal traffic.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include weaving, driving too slowly, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

questions.question: When applying for your driver license, the DMV may test your:
questions.explanation: The DMV will test your vision. You may also take a knowledge exam and a road skills test. A DMV representative will tell you which tests you need to take.
